sections.title: Every proportion: report + name the group

blocks.text: Report as a percentage to **1 decimal place** and name the reference group: **40.0% of commuters**. The course outline says answers without the group lose one point. (S1 reporting rule)

sections.title: Conditional probability + two-way table: choose the denominator

blocks.text: Example counts: among 25 commuters, 10 cycle and 15 do not; among 15 noncommuters, 5 cycle and 10 do not. Total = 40. (Notes sections 1-2; practice Q1)

blocks.setup: Ask first: Among which group? That group is the denominator.

steps.label: Among commuters, what share cycle?
steps.text: 10 / 25 = **40.0% of commuters**. P(cycle | commuter): overlap divided by commuter total.

steps.label: Among cyclists, what share commute?
steps.text: 10 / 15 = **66.7% of cyclists**. P(commuter | cycle): same overlap, different reference group.

steps.label: Row percentage
steps.text: Cell divided by its row total. Each row sums to 100%. Example: commuter/cycle = 10/25 = 40.0%.

steps.label: Column percentage
steps.text: Cell divided by its column total. Each column sums to 100%. Example: commuter/cycle = 10/15 = 66.7%.

blocks.takeaway: P(A | B) means A among B: B supplies the denominator. P(A | B) usually differs from P(B | A). (Notes sections 1.1-1.4, 2.2-2.3)

blocks.prompt: Earlier two-way-table attempt: chose the row total for a column percentage.
blocks.first_error: Used the total for the wrong reference group.
blocks.fix: For a column percentage, divide by that column's total; for a row percentage, divide by that row's total.
blocks.conditions: Name the group represented by the chosen row or column before dividing. Check that row percentages sum across each row and column percentages down each column to 100%. (S2 §2; learning record, T2 attempt 2026-11-17)

blocks.text: Conditional probability requires an equally weighted sample and a nonempty reference group. (S2 §1.4)

blocks.setup: For a mean score by course section, each nonempty section becomes one output row.

steps.label: Rows returned
steps.text: One row per nonempty group. Four nonempty sections = **4 rows**, even if the original data had 120 students. (Notes section 3.2; 2025 past paper Q3)

steps.label: Compare fairly
steps.text: Compare the same summary across groups (mean with mean, count with count); do not compare a group mean with a group total. (S2 §3.3)

blocks.takeaway: Grouping changes the output unit from individual cases to groups. A grouped summary has one summary value per group. (S2 §3.1–3.3)
